name: stair_rules
rows: Comfort stair, no rule of law

name: headroom_edge_limit_x
expr: going_depth * (floor_to_floor - floor_thickness - rule_headroom - rise_height) / rise_height - nosing_length

name: tread_min_for_deflection
expr: pow(stair_point_load * inner_width ^ 2 * 300 / (4 * 0.97 * timber_e_modulus * going_depth) / 1 mm^3, 1 / 3) * 1 mm

name: string_depth_required
expr: pow(5 * stringer_line_load * stringer_design_span ^ 3 * 300 * 12 / (384 * timber_e_modulus * stringer_net_thickness * pitch_cos ^ 2) / 1 mm^3, 1 / 3) * 1 mm

name: stringer_thickness_min
expr: max(30 mm, housing_depth + 5 * stringer_line_load * stringer_design_span ^ 3 * 300 * 12 / (384 * timber_e_modulus * pitch_cos ^ 2 * stringer_board_cap ^ 3))

points: pitch_slope * (baluster_first_x + baluster_size / 2 + nosing_length) + rise_height + handrail_height - rail_path_drop + baluster_tenon
pitch_slope * (baluster_first_x - baluster_size / 2 + nosing_length) + rise_height + handrail_height - rail_path_drop + baluster_tenon

arc: (going_depth + router_radius) * pitch_cos + (((rise_height - tread_thickness) - wedge_taper) + router_radius) * pitch_sin
(((rise_height - tread_thickness) - wedge_taper) + router_radius) * pitch_cos - (going_depth + router_radius) * pitch_sin

line: ((going_depth + riser_thickness + wedge_taper) - router_radius) * pitch_cos + (((rise_height - tread_thickness) - router_radius)) * pitch_sin
(((rise_height - tread_thickness) - router_radius)) * pitch_cos - ((going_depth + riser_thickness + wedge_taper) - router_radius) * pitch_sin

center: ((going_depth + riser_thickness + wedge_taper) - router_radius) * pitch_cos + ((rise_height - tread_thickness)) * pitch_sin
((rise_height - tread_thickness)) * pitch_cos - ((going_depth + riser_thickness + wedge_taper) - router_radius) * pitch_sin

line: (going_depth + riser_thickness) * pitch_cos + ((2 * rise_height - tread_thickness + riser_tongue)) * pitch_sin
((2 * rise_height - tread_thickness + riser_tongue)) * pitch_cos - (going_depth + riser_thickness) * pitch_sin

arc: (top_riser_x + router_radius) * pitch_cos + (((floor_to_floor - rise_height - tread_thickness) - router_radius)) * pitch_sin
(((floor_to_floor - rise_height - tread_thickness) - router_radius)) * pitch_cos - (top_riser_x + router_radius) * pitch_sin

floor_to_floor
label: Floor to floor height
description: From the finished lower floor to the finished upper floor, measured in the stairwell. One flight bridges at most 4 m (Bbl); the Flemish rule allows at most 17 treads without a landing, so at most 3.24 m here.

name: available_run
label: Run you have
description: Horizontal length on the floor, from the face of the upper floor at the top of the stairs back to the wall or door at the foot. The stair, with its newel, takes what it needs up to this. The wall rail runs on at hand height 300 mm past the first nose (400 mm under the Flemish rule).

name: stair_width
label: Stair width
description: Overall width across both stringers: wall to wall, or the stair's outside width. Bbl counts the stringers in the width.

name: floor_thickness
label: Upper floor thickness
description: Floor build-up plus ceiling: from the underside of the ceiling to the finished upper floor. The room below must keep the head height of the rule.

name: opening_length
label: Opening in the upper floor
description: Length of the stairwell opening, measured from the face at the top of the stairs. The smallest opening that keeps the head height is the minimum.

name: building_rule
label: Building rule
description: Which rule the stair must meet: rise, going, step rule, width and handrails follow from it.

name: tread_thickness
label: Tread thickness
description: Oak board thickness of the treads and the landing nosing. The minimum is an orientation only: a 3 kN point load at mid-span on C24 values. A structural engineer must verify the strength.

name: closed_risers
label: Closed risers
description: Risers housed and wedged into the stringers. Off gives an open stair of treads only, with gaps between the treads (see the output): check that this suits the users, children especially.

name: stringer_thickness
label: Stringer thickness
description: Board thickness of the two stringers; at least 18 mm stays behind the 12 mm housings. The minimum keeps a long, wide flight in a board under 480 mm wide on an orientation check; a structural engineer must verify the strength.

name: handrail_style
label: Handrail
description: A wall rail assumes a solid wall behind it, and on a side without a rail a wall or your own barrier: Bbl art. 4.20 requires a fixed barrier where the side drops more than 1 m. The balustrade closes the right side. The Flemish rule allows only wall rails on both sides, because its rails must run on 40 cm past both ends and return to the wall.
choices: Wall rail on the left, wall or barrier on the right
Balustrade on the right, wall rail on the left

name: router_diameter
label: Router bit diameter
description: The CNC bit for the housings: inside corners of the housings are cut to its radius.

title: Wooden stair
author: 3DCraft Jigs
description: A straight closed-string wooden stair for your stairwell. Enter the floor-to-floor height, the run you have, the width and the opening in the upper floor: the Jig chooses the number of steps, the rise and the going by the step rule 2 x rise + going, and keeps them within the dimensions of the rule you pick (rise, going, width, head height and handrail of the Dutch Bbl art. 4.26 and 4.28, the Flemish accessibility code art. 20, or a comfort stair of its own). It checks those dimensions only: fire safety, barriers and fixings are not checked, and the strength figures are an orientation that a structural engineer must verify. Treads and risers are housed in two stringers and held with wedges; wall rails or a balustrade with newel posts follow your choice. How to export for the CNC: select the sketch CNC stringer layout in the Features tab and use File > Export as DXF: the stringer lying along x, its outline and every housing in one drawing, housing depth 12 mm. File > Export, Sheet of set: CNC stringers gives the stringer faces, CNC tread sections the true section of a tread; a STEP of Stringer left, Stringer right and Treads goes to CAM.
